newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil firm, bunker demand good.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil firm, bunker demand good.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil prices were firmer on Monday amid robust demand for bunker fuel oil in northwest Europe and the Mediterranean.

A cargo of bunker fuel, thought to be 380 cst material, was heard sold out of ARA at a hefty $126 cif Canaries, reflecting the cost of freight over ARA prices. High sulphur barges were traded at $115, $115.50, $116 and $116.50 fob ARA.
"There is much more demand for bunker fuel than for utility grades, and there is not much around for January," one U.K.-based refinery dealer said.
One utility player said he saw early offers at around $118 cif NWE and traders said that talk was so thin later prices were notional, despite the 50 cents a barrel gain in crude futures.

Low sulphur prices failed to rise far, amid a perception that Italian buying was likely to be lacklustre in January, and following the sale of a distressed U.K.-origin cargo on Friday at around $120 cif NWE, well below the market. Dealers said swaps numbers were worth around $122 fob NWE by the day's end.
At least four pieces were available in the first half of January, and this perceived length counteracted crude's rise.
